overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance indicates extreme viewer preference for extreme space scenarios, specifically 'What If You Fell Into...' formats and exotic planetary phenomena (diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets). These hooks achieve significantly higher views-per-day and like-to-view ratios compared to general psychology, history, or basic animal facts. The audience favors high-stakes, visually striking, mind-bending cosmic concepts over standard educational trivia.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Cosmic Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) massively outperform standard static fact videos published in the same period.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-stakes hypothetical survival scenarios set in extreme space environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre planetary conditions—such as Venus having a day longer than its year (980 views) and TrES-2b being darker than coal (1,027 views)—drive strong organic engagement and high velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on lesser-known, highly bizarre exoplanets and cosmic anomalies with striking visual properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and generic memory/song loop tricks show very low traction and minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychology and brain hack trivia unless framed as a high-intensity survival or mystery narrative.

weak_patterns.pattern: Static Historical/Science Mysteries Without Clear Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' achieve mediocre baseline views (139 views) with zero comments, failing to hook the short-form audience.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague historical mysteries; ensure any historical or scientific topic leads with an immediate, tangible paradox or shock factor.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Coldest Known Place in the Universe (The Boomerang Nebula)?
